subject: Request: enforce single-model routing for CloudHealth EU production (no-fallback)
messages:
From: Sam Wong <sam.wong@cloudhealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-01-15T08:22:00Z
Subject: Production requirement: EU-only single model, no fallback

Ben —

Thanks for the call this morning. To summarize our legal/security ask for CloudHealth's EU production rollout:

- All inference for EU-regulated customers must be pinned to a single vetted model variant (model:v3-eu-tight).
- No automatic fallback to other model variants or regions is permitted (including in overload or degraded performance scenarios).
- We expect a contractual amendment to reflect the enforcement and auditability of that policy.

This is a blocker for our go-live on Feb 6. Our security team is copied. Can Redwood confirm whether you can enforce a "no-fallback, geo-tethered" routing policy for this account and what E2E tradeoffs (latency/SLO/cost) we should expect?

Sam
Sam Wong
Director, Product & Security Integrations
CloudHealth Systems

---
Attachment: SOC2-CloudHealth-request-2027.pdf (attachment from CloudHealth)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Sam Wong <sam.wong@cloudhealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: 2028-01-15T09:08:00Z
Subject: Re: Production requirement: EU-only single model, no fallback

Sam — thanks for the clear summary. Looping in Product (Laura), PreSales/Enterprise (Karthik), and Security/Compliance (Monica) to scope the technical and contractual implications.

High level ask from CloudHealth: pin to model:v3-eu-tight and prevent any automatic fallback (region or model variant) even during capacity contention. Specific questions we need to answer for your legal and go-live:

1) Can we guardrail routing so requests from EU tenants are forcibly routed to a single model instance/variant?
2) If so, what are the availability and latency implications when that capacity is saturated?
3) What operational controls / monitoring will we expose to CloudHealth for audit purposes?

We'll come back with an internal recommendation + a proposed amendment.

Ben Carter
Enterprise Account Exec, Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Sam Wong <sam.wong@cloudhealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: 2028-01-15T11:35:00Z
Subject: Re: Production requirement: EU-only single model, no fallback

Ben / Sam — quick product perspective. Short answer: technically possible, but it's a high-risk operational pattern and we need to be explicit about tradeoffs.

Details:
- Enforceability: We can add a routing policy to map CloudHealth's EU tenants to model:v3-eu-tight and a "hardlock" flag that disables automatic fallback. That would require a custom rule in our routing plane and a pinned capacity allocation to meet throughput SLOs.
- Availability impact: If pinned capacity is exhausted, requests will queue or fail instead of routing to fallback variants. Our current SLA doesn’t cover failure modes for hardlock policies; we'd need an SLA amendment and a design for burst capacity or reserved Dedicated pool.
- Monitoring & audit: We can provide per-tenant routing logs, token-level latency histograms, and an audit export (S3/Drive) for the pinned policy.

Operational asks from Product/Infra:
- Customer must commit to a minimum reserved capacity (Dedicated or commit plan) for production traffic expected.
- If CloudHealth cannot commit, we propose a safety valve: keep hardlock but allow an explicit "escape hatch" path that requires manual ops approval (not automatic).

Next steps: Karthik, can you share expected qps / peak token rates so we can size a Dedicated pool? Monica — please advise on compliance language. Sam — would CloudHealth consider a reserved capacity commitment to enable the hardlock?

—Laura
VP, Product Management
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Sam Wong <sam.wong@cloudhealth.com>
Date: 2028-01-16T07:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Production requirement: EU-only single model, no fallback

Sam / team — from an AE/contracting perspective, CloudHealth indicated ~120 qps average, 450 qps peak (batched) across EU tenants, with heavy weekend spikes. CloudHealth is open to a monthly commit if we can clearly bound cost uplift.

Proposed commercial options:
1) Dedicated EU pool pinned to model:v3-eu-tight. Monthly reserved capacity priced to cover baseline qps; overflow denied (requests fail) — this meets the "no-fallback" requirement but increases cost certainty for Redwood.
2) Hybrid: Dedicated baseline + small warm standby in a lower-cost variant for emergency manual failover (requires 2-hr ops approval). This would keep automatic fallback disabled.

I'll prepare a redline to the Master Services Agreement and the SOW amendment. If Product wants an emergency manual approval flow, Ops/Infra need a documented playbook.

Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Sam Wong <sam.wong@cloudhealth.com>
Date: 2028-01-17T14:50:00Z
Subject: Re: Production requirement: EU-only single model, no fallback

Thanks all — compliance view: we can support the hardlock but require the following as contract conditions and evidence:

- Customer signs an amendment acknowledging availability tradeoffs and commits to minimum reserved capacity (SOW + pricing).
- Redwood provides quarterly routing audit exports and retains routing logs for 12 months in EU-region storage.
- SOC2 Type II evidence attached (see SOC2-Type2-2027.pdf).
- Operational runbook documenting manual approval path (if hybrid option chosen).

I've attached a draft amendment (proposed-amendment-CLOUDHEALTH.docx) with suggested language (clauses: geo-tethered routing, non-fallback acknowledgement, reserved capacity commitment, audit rights). Legal to follow with final redlines.

Monica Patel
Head of Compliance, Redwood Inference
Attachment: SOC2-Type2-2027.pdf
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Sam Wong <sam.wong@cloudhealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: 2028-01-18T17:04:00Z
Subject: Re: Production requirement: EU-only single model, no fallback

Sam — summary and next steps:

- Redwood can implement a geo-tethered, single-variant enforcement (hardlock) for CloudHealth EU tenants.
- Required actions from CloudHealth: sign amendment, commit to a Reserved Capacity plan (we'll size based on Karthik's numbers), and accept the availability tradeoffs for saturated scenarios.
- Deliverables from Redwood: draft amendment (attached), routing audit export schedule, and an ops runbook for manual emergency failover if you choose the hybrid path.

If that aligns, I'll ask Legal to generate the DocuSign and we'll target a sign-off by Jan 24 to meet your Feb 6 go-live.

Ben Carter
Enterprise Account Exec, Redwood Inference
